The enterprise AI lock-in era may have just ended.

Google introduced the Gemini agent at its Gemini at Work event — a persistent enterprise agent that operates across work surfaces and can select among multiple underlying models. The critical design decision: the agent layer is decoupled from the model layer. Enterprise context and workflows remain stable while the model underneath can change.

This is an architectural choice with massive strategic consequences. Until now, choosing an AI vendor meant coupling your workflows, your data pipelines, and your institutional knowledge to a specific model. Switching costs were high by design. Google just broke that pattern — deliberately.

For CTOs, this introduces a new evaluation framework. The question is no longer which model performs best on benchmarks today. It is which agent layer provides the most durable abstraction over your enterprise context — independent of which foundation model leads next quarter.

The implication is that enterprise AI procurement is splitting into two distinct decisions: agent infrastructure and model selection. Organizations that treat these as separate strategic choices will maintain optionality. Those that continue bundling them will accumulate technical debt that compounds with every model generation.

Atlassian made a parallel move the same week, introducing AMP at Team '26 Europe — giving agents identity, scoped authority, and visible participation inside team workflows. The pattern is clear: the agent layer is becoming the durable enterprise asset. The model is becoming interchangeable compute.
